_meta.description: config-driven model pricing table for erebor-ledger. Keys other than '_meta' are model-id PREFIXES matched via longest-prefix-match against the '.message.model' string found in Claude Code transcripts — not required to be an exact model id. A model id with no matching prefix SHALL be reported as unpriced (N/A) by the script; this file SHALL NOT be extended with a guessed/invented price to make an unmatched model 'go away'.
_meta.fields: input, output, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h, cache_read — each priced separately per spec §4
_meta.cache_write_tier_assumption: Claude Code transcripts carry an explicit usage.cache_creation.{ephemeral_5m_input_tokens,ephemeral_1h_input_tokens} breakdown (verified present on every non-zero cache-write record examined on this machine, 2026-07-27), so erebor_ledger.py prices the two tiers exactly from that breakdown rather than assuming one. A record missing that breakdown (e.g. an older/different transcript schema) falls back to pricing its whole cache-write amount at the 5-minute tier — the prior conservative assumption — and the script warns explicitly when this fallback fires.
_meta.counterfactual_assumption: Counterfactual assumes inline execution would consume the same token volume; this is an estimate, not a measurement.
_meta.long_context_note: Models 4.6 and later include the full 1M-token context window at the standard pricing below, so a model id carrying a '[1m]' / long-context marker needs no separate rate here and SHALL NOT be given a premium entry. (Earlier long-context betas did carry a premium; that is why this is stated rather than assumed.)
_meta.cache_tier_sum_divergence: On a small number of records the cache_creation tier fields do not sum to cache_creation_input_tokens (3 unique (message.id, requestId) keys on this framework's reference machine as of 2026-07-27, appearing across 11 content-block lines). Where they diverge, erebor_ledger.py's COST uses the per-tier breakdown and the report's cache(r/w) write VOLUME cell uses the total; every such key is named in the report's warnings.
_meta.fast_mode_limitation: Fast mode (a separate premium tier: $10 input / $50 output per MTok for Opus 5 and Opus 4.8, applying across the full context window) is NOT modeled by this table or the resolver. Claude Code transcripts may not reveal whether fast mode was active for a given record, so erebor_ledger.py always prices Opus records at standard-tier rates below; a session run under fast mode will be under-priced by this report. This is a disclosed, undetected limitation, not a bug.

claude-mythos-5.note: priced identically to claude-fable-5 per official pricing page

claude-opus-4-0.note: legacy Opus tier. Does NOT cover the dateless 'claude-opus-4' id — this key is not a prefix of it; that id has its own 'claude-opus-4' entry below.

claude-opus-4.note: legacy Opus tier; covers the original dateless 'claude-opus-4' id, which no longer/dated key is a prefix of. Longest-prefix matching keeps the dated variants (claude-opus-4-0/4-1/4-5/4-6/4-7/4-8) on their own longer keys, so this entry only ever catches the dateless id and any future claude-opus-4-* variant with no dedicated key.

next_tier.note: standard pricing takes over from this date — erebor_ledger.py switches automatically based on today's date
